I also read the definitions this file relies on: `CoulombEstimates.Separated` (a conjunction of three `eta ≤ dist ...` conditions), `branchMarginal`, `branchCoupling`, `ae_branchCoupling`, `exists_uniform_compact_separation` and `lintegral_coulombCost_lt_top_of_ae_separated`. In Mathlib I checked that `Measurable.dist`, `Measurable.fst` and `Measurable.snd` carry `@[fun_prop]`. The repo already uses `by fun_prop` for measurability goals involving product projections, for example `SpherePlaneWaveSub.lean:327`.

The other proofs are already short and easy to follow, and I found nothing else worth flagging:
- `compact_components` and `disjoint_components_mono` each use one `Fin.cases`.
- The almost-everywhere bookkeeping in `ae_mem_branchMarginal_components` is explicit and matches the shape of the `branchMarginal` sum.
- The `by exact` wrappers in the `have`s of `exists_ae_separated_branchCoupling` and in `compact_support_and_separation` are minor noise. Changing them is only a matter of taste.

Remaining uncertainty: I could not run Lean. I expect `fun_prop` to close each of the three goals, based on the lemma tags and on similar uses in the repo, but I have not compiled the replacement. I deliberately kept the typed `have`s. That way the outer `measurableSet_le`/`.inter` term never has to work out the distance functions by unfolding `Separated`, which is the step most likely to break if the `have`s were dropped.

have h12 : Measurable (fun t : Triple => dist t.1 t.2.1) :=
    measurable_fst.dist (measurable_fst.comp measurable_snd)
  have h13 : Measurable (fun t : Triple => dist t.1 t.2.2) :=
    measurable_fst.dist (measurable_snd.comp measurable_snd)
  have h23 : Measurable (fun t : Triple => dist t.2.1 t.2.2) :=
    (measurable_fst.comp measurable_snd).dist (measurable_snd.comp measurable_snd)
findings.problem: Each of the three measurability facts is built by hand from `measurable_fst`/`measurable_snd` compositions, such as `(measurable_fst.comp measurable_snd).dist (measurable_snd.comp measurable_snd)`. To check these terms, a reader has to work out which projection chain gives `t.2.1` and which gives `t.2.2`. That is routine bookkeeping. The `have` statements already say exactly what is being proved, so these terms hide the actual argument: the set is an intersection of three sublevel sets of measurable distance functions.
findings.proposed_change:
Keep the three typed `have`s and the final line, but replace each hand-built proof term with `fun_prop`:
```lean
lemma measurableSet_separated (eta : ℝ) :
    MeasurableSet {t : Triple | CoulombEstimates.Separated eta t} := by
  have h12 : Measurable (fun t : Triple => dist t.1 t.2.1) := by fun_prop
  have h13 : Measurable (fun t : Triple => dist t.1 t.2.2) := by fun_prop
  have h23 : Measurable (fun t : Triple => dist t.2.1 t.2.2) := by fun_prop
  exact (measurableSet_le measurable_const h12).inter
    ((measurableSet_le measurable_const h13).inter (measurableSet_le measurable_const h23))
```
findings.benefit: The typed `have`s still state the three distance functions explicitly, so the reader sees the same structure: three measurable distances, three sublevel sets, one intersection. The only thing removed is the projection plumbing, which is a standard `fun_prop` goal (`Measurable.dist`, `Measurable.fst` and `Measurable.snd` are all `@[fun_prop]`). The repo already handles goals like this with `by fun_prop`. The proof also no longer depends on the nesting order of the `Triple` projections.
